outcome: The full classification of graphs with representation number 3 remains open, but since 26 January 2024 several specific graph families have been fully classified with respect to representation number 3: word-representable split graphs and split comparability graphs (Feb 2025), word-representable co-bipartite graphs (Sept 2025), melon graphs and their comparability/line-graph restrictions (submitted Feb 2026), and m×n grid graphs / cylindrical grid graphs for m,n ≥ small bounds (July 2025). No AI system was involved in any of this work.
summary: The Wikipedia bullet asks for a full classification of graphs with representation number 3 (word-representable but not 2-representable). As of the frozen revision this was, and remains today, an open problem with no complete classification — the current live Wikipedia article on word-representable graphs still states 'No classification for graphs with representation number 3 is known.' However, several restrictions of the problem (cases, per §3.1) have been settled in the window. (1) Dwary, Mozhui and Krishna, 'Representation Number of Word-Representable Split Graphs' (arXiv:2502.00872, submitted 2 Feb 2025, revised 27 Apr 2025), prove every word-representable split graph has representation number at most 3 and fully characterize which split graphs and split comparability graphs achieve exactly 3 (vs. 2). (2) Das and Hariharasubramanian, 'Word-Representable Co-Bipartite Graphs...' (arXiv:2509.03064, submitted 3 Sept 2025), prove every word-representable co-bipartite graph has representation number at most 3, and that permutation graphs are exactly the co-bipartite graphs achieving representation number 2 — so all other word-representable co-bipartite graphs are classified as having representation number exactly 3. (3) Mozhui and Krishna, 'Word-Representation of Melon Graphs' (arXiv:2602.14179, submitted 15 Feb 2026), classify melon graphs (and their comparability-graph and line-graph restrictions) by representation number 2 vs 3. (4) Alshammari, Kitaev and Pyatkin, on grid and cylindrical grid graphs (arXiv:2507.16469, submitted 23 Jul 2025), show m×n grid graphs (m≥3, n≥3) and m×n cylindrical grid graphs (m≥2, n≥3) all have representation number exactly 3. I opened and read (via fetch) all four preprints' abstracts/content and found no mention of any AI system, machine learning tool, or automated theorem prover in the research process for any of them — these are traditional human mathematical proofs. Each of these results narrows a sub-case of the general classification (a specific graph class) rather than settling the whole question, so per §3.1 this is scope-preserving 'case' progress, coded partial with resolution_direction confirmed (the settled pieces confirm exactly which members of each family are 3-representable, consistent with what was conjectured/expected — none refute an expectation). No AI involvement of any kind was found anywhere in this research area.
competing_reading: One could argue that because no single result resolves the *general* classification (over all graphs), none of these findings should count and the correct status is 'open'. But §3.1 explicitly says a restriction of the stated question (a class of objects) that gets fully settled counts as a case, normally 'partial' — and each of these papers does fully settle representation-number-2-vs-3 status for its named graph class, so 'partial' is the more faithful classification. It is also possible additional 2024-2026 papers on other graph families (not surfaced by my searches) exist; I searched broadly but arXiv's coverage of this niche subfield is not exhaustively indexed by generic web search.
what_would_settle_it: A paper providing a forbidden-subgraph or structural characterization valid for all graphs (analogous to Gallai's classification of comparability graphs) would fully resolve the general classification and move status to resolved/claimed. Absent that, further family-by-family results would keep it at partial.

events.what: Characterises which word-representable split graphs and split comparability graphs have representation number 3
Grid graphs (m,n>=3) and cylindrical grid graphs (m>=2,n>=3) have representation number exactly 3
Word-representable co-bipartite graphs have representation number at most 3, exactly 2 iff permutation graphs
Classifies melon graphs by representation number 2 vs 3

judgement.doubts: All four events are class-restricted cases of a full classification, so the status is partial whatever their verification. The melon paper appears to have a Graphs and Combinatorics journal version, but the record could not open it. 'Confirmed' is a loose fit for a classification question that has no conjectured answer. The live article still says no classification is known.
